findings.title: A crisis turn is tested after rescue
findings.claim: A crisis invocation can be genuine, yet the focus's guide is characterized by a path of return; 31:32 makes persistence after rescue relevant without deciding that every moderate survivor has turned away.
findings.mechanism: The exact trace moves from covering waves and turbulence to exclusive invocation, rescue, a moderate post-rescue response, and possible betrayal. The wider 39:8 parallel also moves from distress-turning to later forgetting and diversion, returning through the focus's returner and path.
findings.reader_payoff: The unresolved question becomes visible as a test of durable orientation after pressure lifts, while the possible faithfulness of the moderate survivor remains live.
findings.containment: Crisis-return alone is not made false, and the moderate person's standing is not judged; the inference concerns what a guide's traversable path must show. HFT roots, coordinates, and roles remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The exact 31:32 surface and wider parallel are supplied, but HFT roles are legacy attributions; the source itself preserves an alternative reading.

findings.title: Care remains; accountability cannot be transferred
findings.claim: The focus preserves companionship and recognized good within near-world family life, while the later reciprocal statement denies that either generation can stand in for the other at final accounting.
findings.mechanism: 31:33 repeats parent/child non-substitution and warns against deception by the near life; 39:7 links individual responsibility to return and report. These wider triggers return through the focus's pressure, companionship, near-world, and good-conduct words.
findings.reader_payoff: Disagreement need not become abandonment: family closeness still carries care, but it cannot transfer conscience or final responsibility.
findings.containment: The later axiom concerns final accountability and is projected back only as a boundary on substitution, not as a negation of present care. HFT roles remain attributed, and the good-conduct branch is not reduced to a single legal norm.

epistemic.reason: The 31:33 and 39:7 contacts and their HFT roles are legacy contextual evidence without target morphology; the focus care branches provide the return points.

findings.title: Refusal as spatial reorientation
findings.claim: As a deliberately form-distant analogy, refusal of kin-pressure can be pictured as refusing to let that demand become the organizing support of action, while divine beacon and orientation supply another axis.
findings.mechanism: The HFT maps the focus obedience form to a pole/rising image, then contacts the beacon at 31:20 and the oriented face at 31:22. The image returns through the actual focus refusal and following-path relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The refusal gains a spatial picture of reorientation without losing its ordinary command meaning.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory split-root analogy only, never a translation or lexical gloss of تُطِعْهُمَا; the supplied target morphology is absent and the context roles remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT explicitly labels the mapping non-dominant and form-distant; it survives only as a contained analogy anchored by the focus refusal and later orientation imagery.

The root_001464/B002 registry lists root_ar ن و ب and erroneously attaches both 31:15:21:1 أَنَابَ (ROOT:nwb) and 31:15:26:2 أُنَبِّئُ (ROOT:nbA). The report activation is restricted to exact 31:15:26:2 and its matching NBʾ context at 31:23:8; it is not transferred to أَنَابَ.
The small or concealed item in 31:16 could be any matter, not specifically a deed; the return/report/action sequence supports the deed-history reading only as a qualified contextual inference.
At 31:32 the moderate post-rescue person may remain genuinely faithful; persistence sharpens the guide question without ranking that person.
The O03 spatial model is a split-root analogy only, never a translation of تُطِعْهُمَا.
